reviews.title: Current version too difficult to use on mobile
reviews.text: I’ve used this app for a while. The current version adds AI features while making the app harder to use on mobile. For example, on smaller iPhone screens the Undo button is on top of the Save button, and the Redo button is on top of the Layers selector. It’s nearly impossible to click one without accidentally clicking the other. I am not personally interested in trying to use AI, and on a small screen it’s also really hard to avoid accidentally clicking the ChatGPT “helper.” I can move the chatbot icon around but I can’t figure out how to hide it, so no matter what, I keep accidentally clicking it. It’s just really hard to use the app on my phone now, which is disappointing. I think a lot of companies have started investing more in AI than in UX and it really shows in apps like this that are becoming less and less usable.

reviews.title: Too complicated for occasional use
reviews.text:
I am an experienced crafter, and I find Cricut Design Space unnecessarily complicated and frustrating.

Today, I simply wanted to add a person’s name to a birthday card using lettering that matched the existing design. Something that should have taken two minutes became an extended exercise in searching through menus, fonts, and settings.

Why isn’t it obvious how to select a font that writes with a pen rather than outlines the letters? Why is the Writing option hidden under a dropdown labeled Regular?

I love creating things, but I don’t want to become a software expert just to make a greeting card.

Please have your software designers observe ordinary crafters trying to perform simple tasks without assistance. I suspect they would discover how unintuitive this program can be.

Cricut should make crafting more enjoyable, not more stressful.

Please prioritize simplicity and ease of use in future updates.

reviews.title: Windows 11 Cricut Design Space Is a Slow, Bloated, Unusable Nightmare!
reviews.text:
⭐ 0/5

Cricut Design Space for Windows is absolutely horrific! It takes forever to load, constantly runs slowly, and makes even the simplest projects unnecessarily frustrating. Half the battle is getting the software to function long enough to actually design something!

Why isn’t there a Cricut Design Space Lite?

Not everyone pays for Cricut Access, and not everyone wants or needs hundreds of premium features cluttering up the software. Those of us who use our own designs, SVGs, and images should have access to a lightweight version that doesn’t consume so much RAM and struggle with basic tasks.

I shouldn’t need a high-performance computer just to upload an SVG, resize an image, or cut vinyl!

Instead of constantly adding paid features, Cricut should focus on making its software faster, more stable, and actually usable.

Give customers a Design Space Lite option with basic design, upload, print-then-cut, and cutting functions. No unnecessary extras, no constant lag, and no bloated interface.

We purchased the machines. We should be able to use them without fighting the software every step of the way!

reviews.title: Update the Mac app

No way to select which push notifications you can have.  So either all or nothing.

It’s so nice that this app is so frequently updated, the Mac app however is a little bit forgotten.

You’ve frustratingly blocked the iPad app from being used on the Mac, so the only option we have on the Mac is to use the full Mac app. Unfortunately this is still not a universal app and it still needs Rosetta to run.  I’ve just got a new Mac.  Cricut is the ONLY app I use that hasn’t been updated for Apple silicone.  I will not install Rosetta for this 1 app.  It slows my whole machine down.  Please fix the Mac app and I’ll update this review.  You’ve had 5 years to make this a universal app.  There’s about 18 months left before Apple drops Rosetta.  Are you going to wait till the last moment?

And for the love of god, please release some basics for Cricut joy xtra.  We invested in this machine, but you barely supply anything for it.  No white pens to use in black writable material.  No writable material for xtra.  It feels like a con, and whatever is available is ALWAYS out of stock.

reviews.title: New version no longer detects my machine on iPad/iPhone
reviews.text:
(Update on 11 Nov: after updated to ver 6.33, the app completely stopped responding. None of the buttons work, and the whole app is frozen every time I open it. Please fix it ASAP!)

(Update on 21 Aug: The email given by the developer was invalid. I then went to Cricut’s official website and submitted my issue through Technical Support, but they only asked me to call or use online chat, which didn’t fix the problem. I finally found the real solution on Reddit: rename the machine in iPhone/iPad Bluetooth to “CRICUT” and reinstall the app. After that, it connected successfully.)


（Update on 19 Aug: I tried the method suggested by the developer to re-pair the machine, but it still cannot connect on iPad and iPhone. The email address provided by the developer seems to be invalid.)

I’ve really enjoyed using my Cricut Maker with both my iPad and iPhone over the past few years. It’s always been reliable and easy to use. However, after installing the latest version of the Design Space app, I can no longer connect to my machine at all from my mobile devices.

I’ve tried reinstalling the app, restarting both the devices and the machine, but nothing helps. Oddly, it still works fine when I connect it to my MacBook using the desktop app, so it seems like the issue is specific to the current mobile version.

I hope this can be addressed soon in a future update — I’d really love to continue working from my iPad like I used to.
